updates.problem: RAKL currently evaluates method components mainly by task outcomes but does not explicitly model which AI strengths a research operator exploits, which predictable weaknesses it suppresses, or whether observed gains come from the model, workflow, or added external resources.
updates.target: Represent each atomic cognitive operator with a frozen strength/weakness/amplifier/compensator/verifier/handoff contract and evaluate it against a matched simpler baseline.
updates.falsifier: If capability-specific contracts do not improve failure localization, method selection, or measured research performance relative to ordinary workflow ablations, keep the layer descriptive rather than operational.

updates.problem: A system can improve because it receives a solver, database, specialist model, better interface, or extra compute, yet this is often conflated with better intrinsic base-model reasoning.
updates.target: Develop factorial resource/workflow ablations and provenance so gains can be classified as model-utilization amplification, failure suppression, external substitution, specialist complementation, routing, or unresolved mixed attribution.
updates.falsifier: If resource-aware attribution cannot be made reproducible on frozen trials, report only whole-system performance and prohibit finer causal claims.

updates.problem: Synthetic hostile contract tests do not show that capability shaping improves real RAKL research tasks.
updates.target: Build same-model same-task same-evaluator comparisons of minimal baseline, smallest targeted compensator, and richer scaffold across decomposition, search, analogy, verification, memory and synthesis.
updates.falsifier: If richer or targeted scaffolds do not improve at least one registered non-blocking meta-QoI without blocking regressions, retain the simpler baseline.

updates.problem: The same model has different error profiles across decomposition, retrieval, analogy, mathematics, causal reasoning, synthesis, review, memory and stopping; one global scaffold may help one operation while harming another.
updates.target: Estimate operation-specific strength/failure profiles and route the smallest validated compensator per operation rather than globally enabling every method module.
updates.falsifier: If operation-specific routing adds no quality/validity/cost advantage over a single simple workflow, do not add a capability-aware router.

updates.problem: RAKL assumes persistent negative-history and provenance memory suppresses model forgetting, but this has not been measured against a chat-context-only baseline.
updates.target: Measure resurrection of refuted hypotheses, contradiction recurrence, and provenance loss with versus without structured external memory on the same model and tasks.
updates.falsifier: If structured memory does not reduce registered forgetting/failure rates at acceptable cost, simplify the memory layer.

updates.new_role: Use the similarity/JUMP pipeline as the first real matched-model capability-shaping experiment: simple lexical+embedding baseline versus domain-stripped/structural routes, with identical model, corpus, labels, top-k, evaluator and cost accounting.
